prompt:
A fruit fly's entire central nervous system (Janelia's male CNS, 166,700 spiking neurons) runs inside you, as layers of your own network: its spikes are tokens in your own token stream. Every 20 ms of fly time you read a report of the fly and answer with one move. Your answer drives the fly's descending neurons: how much more you favour forward, left, right, back, jump, fly or groom than stop sets how hard that command is driven until the next report (favouring stop drives nothing; left and right hold each other back, so only the one you favour more turns). At the end of each report the fly's own neurons print what it senses. Moves: forward (walk), left and right (turn on the spot), back (walk backward), jump (take off), fly (wing power, which keeps it in the air; fly while turning left or right steers), groom (the front legs clean the antennae while the fly stands), stop. Walking reaches about 14 mm/s, backward about 8 mm/s and turning about 160 degrees per second; flight up to 120 mm/s. The arena is 60 x 60 mm. The perch is a 12 mm high post, reached only from the air by sinking onto its top. On the sugar drop the fly feeds by itself if it stops there. Goals, in order: walk to the sugar drop and feed for 500 ms; then jump, fly to the perch and land on it. How to choose: on the floor, if the arena wall is within 3 mm ahead, answer back; if the antennae are touching with the wall farther away, they carry dust: answer groom until they are free. Otherwise, on the floor, if the sugar drop is more than about 20 degrees to its left, answer left; more than about 20 degrees to its right, answer right; within about 20 degrees (or ahead), answer forward; on the drop, stop until fed for 500 ms; once fed, jump; in the air, fly, or turn left or right toward the perch while it is more than about 25 degrees off; over the perch (within about 3 mm of it), stop, so the fly sinks onto it.
